questions.q: Why did Alan stop at houses along the way during the night, even while fleeing?
choices: To beg for food
To pass on the news of the murder
To ask the people which road the soldiers had taken
To collect the second rent for Ardshiel one last time
questions.evidence: This was to pass the news

questions.q: Which valley does David later think they may have come to at dawn?
choices: Glencoe
Glen Lyon
The Ross
Lochaber
questions.evidence: it may have been the valley called Glencoe

questions.q: How did David react when he found himself standing on the small middle rock in the river?
choices: He laughed and jumped ahead of Alan
He felt sick with fear and covered his eyes
He sat down and refused to go on at all
He shouted for help to some people up on the far bank
questions.evidence: there came on me a deadly sickness of fear, and I put my hand over my eyes

questions.q: What did Alan do just before he shouted "Hang or drown!" and leaped across?
choices: He tied his belt around David's waist
He made David drink some brandy
He threw his sword across to the bank
He pointed out the soldiers on the hill
questions.evidence: Alan had set the brandy bottle to my lips

questions.q: What happened when David leaped across the far branch of the river?
choices: He landed safely on both feet beside Alan
Only his hands reached, and Alan dragged him up
He fell into the water and swam to the bank
He slipped back onto the middle rock and waited there for help
questions.evidence: Alan seized me, first by the hair, then by the collar

questions.q: How did Alan finally get up onto the top of the two great rocks?
choices: By climbing a small birch tree that grew beside them
By standing on David's shoulders and leaping
By throwing his belt over a point of stone
By finding a crack that ran to the top
questions.evidence: by standing on my shoulders and leaping up

questions.q: Why were the two leaning rocks such a good hiding place?
choices: They had a cave underneath where a fire could be lit
Their tops made a hollow dish where men could lie hidden
They stood out in the river, so that no soldier could ever reach them
A spring of cool water ran out from between them
questions.evidence: made a kind of dish or saucer, where as many as three or four men might have lain hidden

questions.q: What did Alan say when David was ashamed of his poor jumping?
choices: That a real Highlander would never have been afraid
That being afraid and doing it anyway makes a fine man
That David must practise his jumping every single day from now on
That he would leave David behind the next time
questions.evidence: To be feared of a thing and yet to do it, is what makes the prettiest kind of a man

questions.q: What two mistakes did Alan blame himself for?
choices: Taking a wrong road and forgetting a water-bottle
Losing the oatmeal and leaving his sword behind
Telling James their plan and trusting the boatman
Sleeping too long and making too much noise
questions.evidence: I have come wanting a water-bottle

questions.q: Alan says, "I have proved myself a gomeral this night," and then lists his mistakes. What is a "gomeral"?
choices: A hero
A fool
A guide
A coward
questions.evidence: I have proved myself a gomeral this night

questions.q: Why did Alan put his hand over David's mouth at about nine in the morning?
choices: David was snoring
David was crying out in a bad dream
David was about to sneeze
David was humming

questions.q: What did David see in the valley when he looked over the edge of the rock?
choices: A camp of red-coats with sentries posted along the river
A band of Campbells with dogs searching every rock
Farmers cutting hay in the fields near the river
A long line of emigrants walking toward the coast
questions.evidence: About half a mile up the water was a camp of red-coats

questions.q: Alan says they must "lie here and birstle," and then the sun beats on them all day. What does "birstle" mean here?
choices: Sleep quietly
Roast in the heat
Keep watch
Hide from the rain

questions.q: Why does David find it strange to suffer on the rock that day?
choices: He had always loved hot summer weather back home
Only days before, he had suffered from cold on his island
He had never been outdoors for a whole day before
Alan had promised him that the rock would be cool
questions.evidence: first from cold upon my island and now from heat upon this rock

questions.q: What did the English soldier say when he touched the rock where they lay?
choices: "There's somebody up there"
"I tell you it's 'ot"
"Search behind this one"
"Fetch me some water"

questions.q: What did Alan and David do at about two in the afternoon, when the heat was beyond bearing?
choices: They ran straight down to the river to drink
They slipped down into the shade on the far side of the rock
They gave themselves up to the nearest sentry
They covered themselves with bracken and stayed put on top of the rock
questions.evidence: slipped over the edge and dropped on the ground on the shadowy side

questions.q: What is "drammach," which they made after drinking at the burn?
choices: Cold water mixed with oatmeal
Brandy warmed over a small fire
Oat-cakes baked on a hot stone
Fish boiled in the iron pan
questions.evidence: it is but cold water mingled with oatmeal

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Alan and David hiding from soldiers on a scorching rock and then escaping
Alan and David being caught by soldiers in Glencoe and breaking free
David leaving Alan behind and going on alone to the Lowlands
Alan teaching David to fight with a sword while they wait
questions.evidence: we drew steadily away from their neighbourhood
